Naming a dimension "method" throws error when calling ".loc"
#### Code Sample, a copy-pastable example if possible

```python
import numpy as np
from xarray import DataArray
empty = np.zeros((2,2))
D1 = DataArray(empty, dims=['dim1', 'dim2'],   coords={'dim1':['x', 'y'], 'dim2':['a', 'b']})
D2 = DataArray(empty, dims=['dim1', 'method'], coords={'dim1':['x', 'y'], 'method':['a', 'b']})

print(D1.loc[dict(dim1='x', dim2='a')])    # works
print(D2.loc[dict(dim1='x', method='a')])  # does not work!! 
```
#### Problem description

The name of the dimension should be irrelevant. The error message 

```
ValueError: Invalid fill method. Expecting pad (ffill), backfill (bfill) or nearest.
```

suggests that at some point the `dims` are given to another method in unsanitized form

lcb.title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
lcb.problem_statement: Given two sorted arrays nums1 and nums2 of size m and n respectively, return the median of the two sorted arrays. The overall run time complexity must be O(log(m+n)).

lcb.title: Regular Expression Matching
lcb.problem_statement: Given an input string s and a pattern p, implement regular expression matching with support for '.' and '*'. '.' matches any single character. '*' matches zero or more of the preceding element. The matching should cover the entire input string (not partial).

lcb.title: Merge k Sorted Lists
lcb.problem_statement: You are given an array of k linked-lists lists, each linked-list is sorted in ascending order. Merge all the linked-lists into one sorted linked-list and return it. Implement in O(N log k) time where N is total number of nodes.

lcb.title: Trapping Rain Water
lcb.problem_statement: Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map where the width of each bar is 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining. Solve in O(n) time and O(1) space using two pointers.

lcb.title: Sliding Window Maximum
lcb.problem_statement: You are given an array of integers nums and an integer k. There is a sliding window of size k which moves from left to right. Return the max value in each window position. Solve in O(n) using a monotonic deque.

lcb.title: Minimum Window Substring
lcb.problem_statement: Given two strings s and t, return the minimum window substring of s such that every character in t (including duplicates) is included in the window. If there is no such substring, return empty string. Solve in O(|s| + |t|) using sliding window with frequency maps.

lcb.title: Word Ladder II
lcb.problem_statement: Given two words beginWord and endWord, and a word list, find all shortest transformation sequences from beginWord to endWord such that each word differs by exactly one letter and each intermediate word is in the word list. Return all such sequences or an empty list if none exists.

lcb.title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
lcb.problem_statement: Design an algorithm to serialize and deserialize a binary tree. Serialization is the process of converting a data structure into a sequence of bits so that it can be stored or transmitted. The encoded string should be decodable back to the original tree structure.

lcb.title: Find Median from Data Stream
lcb.problem_statement: Implement the MedianFinder class that supports two operations: addNum(num) — adds an integer num to the data structure, findMedian() — returns the median of all elements so far. Use two heaps (max-heap + min-heap) for O(log n) add and O(1) median.

lcb.title: Alien Dictionary
lcb.problem_statement: There is a new alien language that uses the English alphabet. However, the order of the letters is unknown. You are given a list of strings words from the alien language's dictionary where words are sorted lexicographically by the rules of this language. Derive the order of letters in this language. Return any valid ordering or '' if invalid.
